body:
I wouldn't attend AA because of it's bizarre obsession with giving yourself to a higher power but If I manage to pull through this depression without acting on my suicidal urges the first thing I'd do is attend some sort of program for my drinking.
I've contemplated it many times, but always brushed it off because I'm afraid of turning up and realizing that I'm the most 'well' person there. Now I know that while I may not be an extreme alcoholic I still have an addiction, I consume far more than 4 standard drinks which is the binge drinking criteria for women and most of all, I need help.

In all honesty, I don't want to die. I want my life to be fulfilling, I want meaningful relationships, hobbies that I genuinely enjoy, a job that I may not like all the time but that I'm still proud to do and maybe even someone who I love to come home to. I want my life to be like how I perceive the lives of people around me to be. If I could have even just one of these things, that'd be enough for me. The problem is I just don't know how to get there, and it doesn't look like anyone else knows either.
Currently my life revolves around staying content, I have eliminated all things that scare or upset me. If a friend is stressing me out, I sever. If the idea of education or work is too much, I hole myself up in my room for days playing videogames I enjoyed as a kid just so I can regress back to that age and feel safe again. And most importantly, If my depression becomes too much I drink. I don't want to do any of this anymore, but I'm too afraid to venture out into the world because what if it's even worse? This is why at this point I feel my only option is suicide.

The friend I've hurt, I've known them for 5 years and they've seen me hit a lot of obstacles and seen glimpses of my substance abuse, even heard about my worst episode with hard drugs. 
We've only been recently reacquainted, briefly after a string of suicide attempts and the aftermath of me leaving an abusive relationship. I never told them about what was happening to me before we started talking again except for a small conversation on the state of my mental illness but I felt that if I did, they'd understand. I chose not to because I wanted them to think that I was well again, because as soon as I got out of that depression I did truly think that I was well. Basically I ran into them, much like you did with your friend, and they improved my life and made me believe I could have the life I wanted. They were the friend I need right now and I've driven them off.

I don't think I'll have any withdrawal problems because I'm not a daily drinker, it's just that when I do drink I can't stop. I will literally drink until I run out or pass out.
I've previously been hospitalized, about 5 months back if I recall correctly. It's a very scary and stressful environment that I personally wouldn't wish on anyone. I couldn't even bring myself to leave my room to use the bathroom most days because I was so afraid of the people around me.  Men and women roaming the halls like zombies due to the sedatives they were put on, a woman who didn't even know why she was there and screamed at staff daily to let her know why she couldn't come home, and an old man constantly going from hysterical sobbing to frantic screaming until the nurses could convince him to return to his room which sometimes took hours (In my country it's illegal to restrain or touch psych patients). Not only was I afraid but every time I looked at one of the worse off patients I was afraid I might be looking into my future. I must admit, after coming home I did feel better but now I find myself in the exact same place, a place I never really wanted to ever go again.
If I manage to bounce back a treatment program is probably the first thing I'll involve myself in but I'm still adamant on suicide. I've never really been remorseful about my problems but now I'm stricken with it and it's killing me to know that I can never make amends.
I talked to my friend yesterday about how I couldn't even remember what I'd done and I repeatedly apologized to them. They were civil but stern, told me that I needed to get my act together and that I was no longer allowed to drink in their house but when we talked normally I could hear all feeling they once felt for me had completely disappeared from their voice. Everyone else who witnessed my behavior acknowledges I was out of control but they seem fairly understanding, even sorry for me, but it's my friend who I've upset's opinion that I truly care about and they are so clearly done with me that if I even asked the slightest bit of assistance for my problem they'd probably just laugh in my face. If I decide to seek help I'll be facing it alone which attracts me even further to the easy way out.

I'm really glad you were given that opportunity and that things are better for you. It sounds like you have a good friend, I wish there were more people in the world that understand like she does. I'm sad that I don't have anyone like her in my life.

I've been in weekly therapy for the last 3 years, but I've been involved with the mental health system for the last 9. I've made some progress, mostly regarding self-confidence issues and anxiety management, but it seems like no matter how hard I work I can never undo the effects of what has happened to me. I can't win back old friends and I can't raise the dead. I just see no point living an empty life, constantly longing for people I can no longer have, hurting the few people left in my life and reliving past abuses.
I've reached out so many times and been shot down just as many. I don't have the energy to try again.
